fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Public Versus Private Capacity", "body": "James Frosch opened his slideshow with the claim that everyone is always a private individual, a living man or woman on the land, and that dealing with government happens in a public capacity entered through behavior. He argued that birth certificates, Social Security numbers and benefits were public law instruments, and that accepting them drew a person into that venue. One speaker claimed that even a polite label such as sir could act as a bribe into the public. James said he was not a law expert and urged listeners to read the source texts themselves."}, {"title": "Natural Law and Man's Law", "body": "James explained natural law as the seven Hermetic principles, beginning with mentalism, and described man's law as agreements and guardrails layered on top. He said he had no quarrel with most man's law but objected to institutions that used it to take attention and life force. One speaker added that government, which means mind control, also meant life force control. One speaker described natural law as harsh but humbling, since only truth could stand before it, and a guest framed studying law as a spiritual path."}, {"title": "Gangs, Government and Remedy", "body": "A speaker asked how the non-aggression principle and the golden rule fit a world with bullies, racketeers and a government that works like the largest gang. Another speaker answered that every developmental phase of consciousness had to be lived through, and that the obstacle becomes the path. James replied that victors tended to hide their faces, that parasites were eventually dealt with, and that behavior was what would set people free. Later he read the equity maxim that a wrong never lacks a remedy, which he said usually lay in behavior."}, {"title": "Money, Instruments and Collateral", "body": "Reading from 12 USC and the Uniform Commercial Code, James argued that Federal Reserve notes were negotiable instruments, that money was created through promises to pay, and that a birth certificate could be collateralized and monetized. He said some groups claimed a lawful money remedy and was careful to add that he did not know whether it worked. One speaker noted that collateral also had a genealogical meaning, relatives descended collaterally. Gabe linked the discussion to the Smith-Mundt Modernization Act and what he called a newly mutable age."}, {"title": "Trusts, Legacy and Ecclesiastical Roots", "body": "James closed by urging listeners to run business through an entity rather than a personal name and to learn trust law as a way to hold property for later generations. He described a trustee as the one who executes the trust and trains the next. A speaker argued that the judge and the astronomer priest, the magi, belonged to one ecclesiastical system, and Chance promoted Dylan Saccoccio's Spirit Whirled books. A speaker offered word studies on Barcelona, circumcise and circumscribe. Chance called the episode a first part of a longer conversation."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Topher Gardner of the BioCharisma Podcast returns along with James Frosch of Family Fungi. We plan to discuss our creative, divine spark, and what that means for our jurisdiction as parents and families in Babylon, and in Nature.
